+	"context"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"strings"
+
+	"charm.land/huh/v2"
+
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck"
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo"
+)
+
+// cliUpgradeRequiredCode is the OAuth error code the server returns when
+// this CLI build is older than the minimum version it accepts.
+const cliUpgradeRequiredCode = "cli_upgrade_required"
+
+// cliUnsupportedMsg leads every cli_upgrade_required guidance block,
+// followed by the update command, then a "Then rerun the command:" block
+// with the command that failed.
+const cliUnsupportedMsg = "This Entire CLI version is no longer supported. Update it:"
+
+// IsCLIUpgradeRequired reports whether err carries the server's
+// cli_upgrade_required OAuth error code. auth-go surfaces the code as an
+// unrecognised-code error whose message carries it verbatim — there is no
+// sentinel to errors.Is against, so match on the code string.
+func IsCLIUpgradeRequired(err error) bool {
+	return err != nil && strings.Contains(err.Error(), cliUpgradeRequiredCode)
+}
+
+// upgradeOfferDeps carries the environment-dependent pieces of
+// offerCLIUpgrade so tests can drive both branches without a TTY, a
+// real installer, or replacing the test process. Zero-value fields are
+// safe: nil confirm declines, and nil runUpdate is never reached
+// without confirm.
+type upgradeOfferDeps struct {
+	canPrompt func() bool
+	confirm   func(ctx context.Context, updateCmd string) (bool, error)
+	runUpdate func(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer, cmdStr string, argv []string)
+}
+
+// OfferCLIUpgradeIfRequired handles a cli_upgrade_required failure in
+// place of the raw error print: it reports true when it took over the
+// messaging (main.go then skips printing err — the raw OAuth chain adds
+// nothing the guidance doesn't say), false when err doesn't carry the
+// code. On an interactive terminal it offers to run the updater right
+// away and, on success, re-executes the original command with the
+// freshly installed binary (the shared versioncheck.RunUpdate tail, also
+// used by the version-check prompt); otherwise — no TTY,
+// ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE set, declined, or no runnable installer for this
+// platform — it prints the update command and the failed command so the
+// user can run both. argv is the failed invocation's os.Args.
+//
+// The code can surface from any auth-server OAuth flow — login (device
+// and browser), the refresh grant under every authenticated command, and
+// the RFC 8693 exchanges — which is why this hangs off main.go's central
+// error-print arm rather than any single command.
+func OfferCLIUpgradeIfRequired(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer, err error, argv []string) bool {
+	return offerCLIUpgrade(ctx, w, err, argv, upgradeOfferDeps{
+		canPrompt: func() bool { return versioncheck.PromptAllowed(w) },
+		confirm:   confirmCLIUpgrade,
+		runUpdate: versioncheck.RunUpdate,
+	})
+}
+
+func offerCLIUpgrade(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer, err error, argv []string, deps upgradeOfferDeps) bool {
+	if !IsCLIUpgradeRequired(err) {
+		return false
+	}
+	updateCmd := versioncheck.UpdateCommandForCurrentBinary(versioninfo.Version)
+	rerun := versioncheck.RerunCommandLine(argv)
+
+	// Post-update rerun still rejected: the installer wrote somewhere
+	// other than the binary this invocation ran (e.g. a dev build outside
+	// the install manager's path). Saying "update it" again would be
+	// wrong — the update already happened; name the actual problem.
+	// (PromptAllowed also blocks on this marker, but this branch replaces
+	// the whole guidance block, not just the prompt.)
+	if versioncheck.IsPostUpdateRerun() {
+		binary := "this binary"
+		if len(argv) > 0 {
+			binary = argv[0]
+		}
+		fmt.Fprintf(w, "The update installed, but this command still ran an unsupported binary (%s).\nCheck that `entire` on your PATH points at the updated install, then rerun:\n\n  %s\n", binary, rerun)
+		return true
+	}
+
+	if !deps.canPrompt() {
+		printCLIUpgradeCommands(w, updateCmd, rerun)
+		return true
+	}
+
+	confirmed, confirmErr := deps.confirm(ctx, updateCmd)
+	if confirmErr != nil || !confirmed {
+		// Declined or the prompt itself failed/was aborted — leave the
+		// copyable commands either way.
+		printCLIUpgradeCommands(w, updateCmd, rerun)
+		return true
+	}
+
+	deps.runUpdate(ctx, w, updateCmd, argv)
+	return true
+}
+
+// printCLIUpgradeCommands prints the non-interactive guidance block: the
+// update command, then the command that failed, each ready to copy.
+func printCLIUpgradeCommands(w io.Writer, updateCmd, rerun string) {
+	fmt.Fprintf(w, "%s\n\n  %s\n", cliUnsupportedMsg, updateCmd)
+	if rerun != "" {
+		fmt.Fprintf(w, "\nThen rerun the command:\n\n  %s\n", rerun)
+	}
+}
+
+// confirmCLIUpgrade renders the Yes/No update prompt. Abort (Ctrl-C,
+// timeout) surfaces as an error and the caller falls back to printing
+// the commands.
+func confirmCLIUpgrade(ctx context.Context, updateCmd string) (bool, error) {
+	confirmed := true
+	form := NewAccessibleForm(huh.NewGroup(
+		huh.NewConfirm().
+			Title("This Entire CLI version is no longer supported.").
+			Description(fmt.Sprintf("Update now? (runs `%s`)", updateCmd)).
+			Value(&confirmed),
+	))
+	if err := form.RunWithContext(ctx); err != nil {
+		return false, fmt.Errorf("update prompt: %w", err)
+	}
+	return confirmed, nil
+}

+package versioncheck
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"errors"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"os"
+	"os/exec"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"strconv"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/interactive"
+)
+
+// This file is the single update flow shared by both update triggers:
+// the version-check nag (MaybeAutoUpdate) and the server's
+// cli_upgrade_required rejection (package cli). The triggers differ only
+// in how they detect the condition and which prompt they show — the gate
+// (PromptAllowed) and everything after the user accepts (RunUpdate) live
+// here once.
+
+// envUpgradeRerun marks a process re-executed after a successful update.
+// If that rerun still fails or still looks outdated (the installer updated
+// a different binary than the one running), prompts are suppressed so an
+// ineffective update can't loop forever.
+const envUpgradeRerun = "ENTIRE_UPGRADE_RERUN"
+
+// reexec is a test seam for re-executing the original command.
+var reexec = realReexecCommand
+
+// IsPostUpdateRerun reports whether this process was re-executed by
+// RunUpdate after an update. Callers use it to replace "update it" advice
+// with a stale-binary explanation.
+func IsPostUpdateRerun() bool {
+	return os.Getenv(envUpgradeRerun) != ""
+}
+
+// PromptAllowed is the single gate for showing an interactive update
+// prompt, shared by both triggers: never with the kill switch set or on a
+// post-update rerun (loop guard), and only with a runnable installer on
+// an interactive terminal.
+func PromptAllowed(w io.Writer) bool {
+	return os.Getenv(envKillSwitch) == "" &&
+		!IsPostUpdateRerun() &&
+		canAutoInstall() &&
+		interactive.CanPromptInteractively() &&
+		isTerminalOut(w)
+}
+
+// RunUpdate is the shared execution tail after the user accepts an update
+// offer: it announces the installer command, runs it, and reports failure
+// with a copyable retry command. On success, a nil argv just tells the
+// user to re-run entire (the version-check trigger fires after the
+// command already completed — re-executing would run it twice); a non-nil
+// argv is re-executed with the freshly installed binary (the
+// cli_upgrade_required trigger fires after the command failed, so the
+// rerun is a retry). On a successful re-exec the process exits with the
+// child's exit code and this function does not return.
+func RunUpdate(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer, cmdStr string, argv []string) {
+	fmt.Fprintf(w, "\nUpdating Entire CLI: %s\n", cmdStr)
+	if err := runInstaller(ctx, cmdStr); err != nil {
+		fmt.Fprintf(w, "Update failed: %v\nTry again later running:\n  %s\n", err, cmdStr)
+		return
+	}
+	if len(argv) == 0 {
+		fmt.Fprintln(w, "Update complete. Re-run entire to use the new version.")
+		return
+	}
+	rerun := RerunCommandLine(argv)
+	fmt.Fprintf(w, "Update complete. Rerunning the command:\n\n  %s\n\n", rerun)
+	if err := reexec(ctx, argv); err != nil {
+		fmt.Fprintf(w, "Could not rerun automatically (%v). Rerun the command:\n\n  %s\n", err, rerun)
+	}
+}
+
+// realReexecCommand reruns the original invocation with the freshly
+// installed binary: argv[0] is re-resolved (through PATH when bare, or
+// the same path the installer just replaced) and the child inherits the
+// terminal, so interactive flows like the login prompts still work. The
+// envUpgradeRerun marker suppresses further update prompts if the rerun
+// fails the same way. On success this does not return — the process
+// exits with the child's exit code. A spawn-and-exit is used instead of
+// syscall.Exec so the one code path covers Windows too.
+func realReexecCommand(ctx context.Context, argv []string) error {
+	if len(argv) == 0 {
+		return errors.New("original command unknown")
+	}
+	path, err := exec.LookPath(argv[0])
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("locate %s: %w", argv[0], err)
+	}
+	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, path, argv[1:]...)
+	cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin
+	cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
+	cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
+	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), envUpgradeRerun+"=1")
+	if runErr := cmd.Run(); runErr != nil {
+		if exitErr, ok := errors.AsType[*exec.ExitError](runErr); ok {
+			os.Exit(exitErr.ExitCode())
+		}
+		return fmt.Errorf("rerun command: %w", runErr)
+	}
+	os.Exit(0)
+	return nil
+}
+
+// RerunCommandLine reconstructs an invocation for display: argv[0]
+// reduced to its base name, arguments with shell-significant whitespace
+// or quotes quoted so the line can be pasted back verbatim.
+func RerunCommandLine(argv []string) string {
+	if len(argv) == 0 {
+		return ""
+	}
+	parts := make([]string, 0, len(argv))
+	parts = append(parts, filepath.Base(argv[0]))
+	for _, a := range argv[1:] {
+		if strings.ContainsAny(a, " \t\"'") {
+			a = strconv.Quote(a)
+		}
+		parts = append(parts, a)
+	}
+	return strings.Join(parts, " ")
+}

+// unrecognised-code error whose message carries it verbatim — there is no
+// sentinel to errors.Is against, so match on the code string.

+			Description(fmt.Sprintf("Update now? (runs `%s`)", updateCmd)).

+		return false, fmt.Errorf("update prompt: %w", err)
+	}

+}

+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"errors"

+	"path/filepath"
+	"strconv"
+	"strings"

+// This file is the single update flow shared by both update triggers:
+// the version-check nag (MaybeAutoUpdate) and the server's
+// cli_upgrade_required rejection (package cli). The triggers differ only
+// in how they detect the condition and which prompt they show — the gate
+// (PromptAllowed) and everything after the user accepts (RunUpdate) live
+// here once.
+
+// envUpgradeRerun marks a process re-executed after a successful update.
+// If that rerun still fails or still looks outdated (the installer updated
+// a different binary than the one running), prompts are suppressed so an
+// ineffective update can't loop forever.
+const envUpgradeRerun = "ENTIRE_UPGRADE_RERUN"
+
+// reexec is a test seam for re-executing the original command.
+var reexec = realReexecCommand
+
+// IsPostUpdateRerun reports whether this process was re-executed by
+// RunUpdate after an update. Callers use it to replace "update it" advice
+// with a stale-binary explanation.
+func IsPostUpdateRerun() bool {
+	return os.Getenv(envUpgradeRerun) != ""
+}
+
+// PromptAllowed is the single gate for showing an interactive update
+// prompt, shared by both triggers: never with the kill switch set or on a
+// post-update rerun (loop guard), and only with a runnable installer on
+// an interactive terminal.
+func PromptAllowed(w io.Writer) bool {
+	return os.Getenv(envKillSwitch) == "" &&
+		!IsPostUpdateRerun() &&
+		canAutoInstall() &&
+		interactive.CanPromptInteractively() &&
+		isTerminalOut(w)
+}
+
+// RunUpdate is the shared execution tail after the user accepts an update
+// offer: it announces the installer command, runs it, and reports failure
+// with a copyable retry command. On success, a nil argv just tells the
+// user to re-run entire (the version-check trigger fires after the
+// command already completed — re-executing would run it twice); a non-nil
+// argv is re-executed with the freshly installed binary (the
+// cli_upgrade_required trigger fires after the command failed, so the
+// rerun is a retry). On a successful re-exec the process exits with the
+// child's exit code and this function does not return.
+func RunUpdate(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer, cmdStr string, argv []string) {
+	fmt.Fprintf(w, "\nUpdating Entire CLI: %s\n", cmdStr)
+	if err := runInstaller(ctx, cmdStr); err != nil {
+		fmt.Fprintf(w, "Update failed: %v\nTry again later running:\n  %s\n", err, cmdStr)
+		return
+	}
+	if len(argv) == 0 {
+		fmt.Fprintln(w, "Update complete. Re-run entire to use the new version.")
+		return
+	}
+	rerun := RerunCommandLine(argv)
+	fmt.Fprintf(w, "Update complete. Rerunning the command:\n\n  %s\n\n", rerun)
+	if err := reexec(ctx, argv); err != nil {
+		fmt.Fprintf(w, "Could not rerun automatically (%v). Rerun the command:\n\n  %s\n", err, rerun)
+	}
+}
+
+// realReexecCommand reruns the original invocation with the freshly
+// installed binary: argv[0] is re-resolved (through PATH when bare, or
+// the same path the installer just replaced) and the child inherits the
+// terminal, so interactive flows like the login prompts still work. The
+// envUpgradeRerun marker suppresses further update prompts if the rerun
+// fails the same way. On success this does not return — the process
+// exits with the child's exit code. A spawn-and-exit is used instead of
+// syscall.Exec so the one code path covers Windows too.
+func realReexecCommand(ctx context.Context, argv []string) error {
+	if len(argv) == 0 {
+		return errors.New("original command unknown")
+	}
+	path, err := exec.LookPath(argv[0])
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("locate %s: %w", argv[0], err)
+	}
+	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, path, argv[1:]...)
+	cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin
+	cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
+	cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
+	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), envUpgradeRerun+"=1")
+	if runErr := cmd.Run(); runErr != nil {
+		if exitErr, ok := errors.AsType[*exec.ExitError](runErr); ok {
+			os.Exit(exitErr.ExitCode())
+		}
+		return fmt.Errorf("rerun command: %w", runErr)
+	}
+	os.Exit(0)
+	return nil
+}
+
+// RerunCommandLine reconstructs an invocation for display: argv[0]
+// reduced to its base name, arguments with shell-significant whitespace
+// or quotes quoted so the line can be pasted back verbatim.
+func RerunCommandLine(argv []string) string {
+	if len(argv) == 0 {
+		return ""
+	}
+	parts := make([]string, 0, len(argv))
+	parts = append(parts, filepath.Base(argv[0]))
+	for _, a := range argv[1:] {
+		if strings.ContainsAny(a, " \t\"'") {
+			a = strconv.Quote(a)
+		}
+		parts = append(parts, a)
+	}
+	return strings.Join(parts, " ")
+}

27		autoUpdateActionUpdate               AutoUpdateAction = "update"
28		autoUpdateActionSkipUntilNextVersion AutoUpdateAction = "skip_until_next_version"

43	// MaybeAutoUpdate prints an update notification and offers an interactive
44	// upgrade. Silent on every failure path — it must never interrupt the CLI.
45	//
46	// The same 3-option prompt (update / skip / skip until next version) is
47	// shown for every install manager that supports auto-installation
48	// (brew, mise, scoop, curl-bash). The only thing that varies between

51	// If the installer command fails, a hint with the exact command is

3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"fmt"
7		"os"
8		"os/signal"
9		"runtime"
10		"strings"
11		"syscall"
12		"time"

14		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli"
15		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/api"
16		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo"
17		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/procsignal"
18		"github.com/spf13/cobra"
19	)
20	
21	func main() {
22		// Resolve version/commit from build info before anything reads them.
23		versioninfo.Load()
24	
25		// Create context that cancels on interrupt
26		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
27	
28		// Handle interrupt signals
29		sigChan := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
30		signals := []os.Signal{os.Interrupt}
31		if runtime.GOOS != "windows" {
32			signals = append(signals, syscall.SIGTERM)
33		}
34		signal.Notify(sigChan, signals...)
35		go func() {
36			// First signal: cancel the context so in-flight work unwinds
37			// cleanly. signal.Notify has disabled Go's default "signal
38			// terminates" behavior, so without the second read below a user
39			// who Ctrl-C's again during a slow/stuck shutdown (e.g. a keyring
40			// read blocked in a subprocess we can't cancel) would find every
41			// further Ctrl-C swallowed. The second read restores an escape
42			// hatch: signal again to force-exit.
43			//
44			// We remember which signal fired so the eventual termination
45			// re-raises that same signal — a SIGTERM (from a supervisor /
46			// container stop) must exit 143, not masquerade as a SIGINT 130.
47			sig := <-sigChan
48			procsignal.Store(sig)
49			if sig == os.Interrupt {
50				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "\nInterrupting… press Ctrl-C again to force quit.")
51			} else {
52				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "\nReceived termination signal, shutting down… signal again to force quit.")
53			}
54			cancel()
55			<-sigChan
56			dieFromSignal(sig)
57		}()
58	
59		// Create and execute root command
60		rootCmd := cli.NewRootCmd()
61	
62		// Make managed-installed plugins discoverable by the kubectl-style
63		// dispatcher: prepend the managed bin dir to PATH before resolution.
64		// Idempotent and silent on failure (managed installs simply won't be
65		// found this run; PATH-installed plugins still work). The closure
66		// restores PATH so built-in commands and their subprocesses don't
67		// inherit the prepended dir. When a plugin runs, we skip the restore
68		// — the os.Exit ends the process, and the plugin child intentionally
69		// inherits the prepended PATH so it can spawn sibling managed plugins.
70		restorePATH := cli.PrependPluginBinDirToPATH(ctx)
71	
72		if handled, code := cli.MaybeRunPlugin(ctx, rootCmd, os.Args[1:]); handled {
73			cancel()
74			os.Exit(code)
75		}
76		restorePATH()
77	
78		// Retired env vars fail every built-in command up front; a removed knob
79		// must never be silently ignored. Plugins (above) are exempt — what they
80		// read is their business.
81		if err := api.RejectRemovedAuthEnv(); err != nil {
82			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
83			cancel()
84			os.Exit(1)
85		}
86	
87		executed, err := rootCmd.ExecuteContextC(ctx)
88		if err != nil {
89			var silent *cli.SilentError
90	
91			switch {
92			case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) && procsignal.Load() != nil:
93				// A signal cancelled the root context (our handler fired) or a
94				// keyring read was aborted by Ctrl-C. Don't dump the raw
95				// transport/keyring cancellation string ("...: context canceled",
96				// "read access token: signal: interrupt") as if it were a failure
97				// — die quietly by re-raising the signal that triggered it (see
98				// dieFromSignal) so an enclosing `while ...; do entire; done` loop
99				// actually breaks on a single Ctrl-C, and a SIGTERM shutdown still
100				// exits 143.
101				//
102				// We gate on a signal having been recorded rather than on the
103				// error type alone: a context.Canceled that arose without a signal
104				// (e.g. an internally-cancelled sub-context) is a genuine error
105				// and must fall through to normal reporting, not masquerade as a
106				// user abort (which would also wrongly break an enclosing loop).
107				// procsignal is the shared source of truth written both by the
108				// handler above and by the keyring interrupt path; the latter
109				// records the signal on this same goroutine before returning, so
110				// this Load never races that write.
111				cancel()
112				dieFromSignal(terminatingSignal())
113			case errors.As(err, &silent):
114				// Command already printed the error
115			case strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unknown command") || strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unknown flag"):
116				showSuggestion(rootCmd, err)
117			case isPositionalArgError(err):
118				// Arg-count errors come from cobra's own validators (e.g.
119				// cobra.ExactArgs) and surface as "accepts N arg(s), received M".
120				// Show the failing subcommand's usage so the user sees what it
121				// actually expects — rootCmd's usage isn't useful for a
122				// subcommand-level arg mismatch. ExecuteContextC returns the
123				// deepest matched command, which is the one that failed.
124				showSuggestion(executed, err)
125			default:
126				// A server can reject any authenticated flow (login, token
127				// refresh, RFC 8693 exchange) because this build is too old.
128				// The handler replaces the raw cli_upgrade_required error with
129				// actionable guidance — an interactive update offer, or the
130				// update + rerun commands. Handled here so every command gets
131				// it without wrapping its own errors.
132				if !cli.OfferCLIUpgradeIfRequired(ctx, rootCmd.OutOrStderr(), err, os.Args) {
133					fmt.Fprintln(rootCmd.OutOrStderr(), err)
134				}
135			}
136	
137			cancel()
138			os.Exit(1)
139		}
140		if cli.ShouldCheckCheckpointPolicyWarning(executed) {
141			cli.WarnCheckpointPolicyIfNeeded(ctx, rootCmd.ErrOrStderr(), versioninfo.Version)
142		}
143		cancel() // Cleanup on successful exit
144	}
145	
146	// terminatingSignal returns the signal that cancelled the root context,
147	// defaulting to SIGINT when the cancellation came from something other than a
148	// recorded terminating signal (so a stray context.Canceled still exits 130).
149	// The recorded signal lives in the shared procsignal package, written by the
150	// handler goroutine (SIGINT/SIGTERM) and by the keyring interrupt path (SIGINT).
151	func terminatingSignal() os.Signal {
152		if s := procsignal.Load(); s != nil {
153			return s
154		}
155		return os.Interrupt
156	}
157	
158	// dieFromSignal terminates the process as if it had been killed by sig, rather
159	// than exiting normally. The distinction matters to an interactive shell: it
160	// only aborts a `while true; do entire ...; done` loop when the child is
161	// *killed by* SIGINT (WIFSIGNALED). A plain os.Exit(130) is an ordinary exit,
162	// so the loop keeps respawning entire and Ctrl-C never escapes it. Re-raising
163	// the actual signal also keeps a SIGTERM shutdown reporting the conventional
164	// 143 (not 130). We reset sig to its default disposition, re-raise it to
165	// ourselves, and briefly wait for delivery; if the re-raise can't be delivered
166	// (e.g. Windows, where signal-to-self is unsupported) we fall back to a
167	// conventional 128+signal exit so we never hang.
168	func dieFromSignal(sig os.Signal) {
169		signal.Reset(sig)
170		if p, err := os.FindProcess(os.Getpid()); err == nil {
171			if err := p.Signal(sig); err == nil {
172				time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond) // signal delivery ends the process well before this elapses
173			}
174		}
175		os.Exit(exitCodeForSignal(sig))
176	}
177	
178	// exitCodeForSignal maps a signal to the conventional 128+signum exit code
179	// (130 for SIGINT, 143 for SIGTERM), falling back to 130 for a signal that
180	// doesn't carry a numeric value on this platform.
181	func exitCodeForSignal(sig os.Signal) int {
182		if s, ok := sig.(syscall.Signal); ok {
183			return 128 + int(s)
184		}
185		return 130
186	}
187	
188	// isPositionalArgError reports whether err looks like a cobra positional-
189	// arg validator failure. cobra's stock validators (ExactArgs, NoArgs,
190	// MinimumNArgs, MaximumNArgs, RangeArgs) all surface error strings
191	// containing "arg(s)", and that substring doesn't appear in cobra's other
192	// error paths or in the cli's own errors — so it's a stable, cheap
193	// discriminator without reaching into cobra internals.
194	func isPositionalArgError(err error) bool {
195		return strings.Contains(err.Error(), "arg(s)")
196	}
197	
198	func showSuggestion(cmd *cobra.Command, err error) {
199		// Print usage first (brew style)
200		fmt.Fprint(cmd.OutOrStderr(), cmd.UsageString())
201		fmt.Fprintf(cmd.OutOrStderr(), "\nError: Invalid usage: %v\n", err)
202	}

# PR 1794 Review — `cli_upgrade_required` update hint

Verified locally: branch matches PR head, builds clean, all new tests pass.

## Overview

Server rejects old CLI with OAuth code `cli_upgrade_required` from any auth flow (login, refresh grant, RFC 8693). Before: raw error, no path forward. Now: central handler at `main.go` error arm replaces raw error with update offer (interactive) or copyable update+rerun commands (non-interactive). Refactor extracts shared update tail into `versioncheck/updateflow.go` (`PromptAllowed` gate + `RunUpdate`), reused by existing version-check nag. Re-exec after update marked with `ENTIRE_UPGRADE_RERUN=1` — loop guard prevents infinite update→rerun cycles, and stale-binary message names actual problem when installer wrote different file than running binary.

## Correctness — solid

- **Loop guard ordering right**: `IsPostUpdateRerun` checked before `canPrompt` in `offerCLIUpgrade`, so rerun child never re-prompts and gets stale-binary explanation instead of "update it" again.
- **Exit codes right**: successful re-exec exits with child code (`os.Exit(exitErr.ExitCode())` / `os.Exit(0)`); every failure leaf falls back to `main.go`'s `os.Exit(1)`. Installer failure skips rerun. Matches PR claims.
- **`errors.AsType[*exec.ExitError]`**: Go 1.26 API, go.mod says 1.26.4, compiles. Fine.
- **`MaybeAutoUpdate` gate swap safe**: `canAutoInstall()` inside `PromptAllowed` is redundant there (checked earlier at versioncheck.go:65) but harmless. Added `!IsPostUpdateRerun()` is intentional — suppresses version-check re-prompt right after update. Correct.
- **Switch arm ordering**: `SilentError` arm precedes default, so curated-message paths bypass handler — documented, acceptable gap.
- **Windows+unknown installer**: `UpdateCommandForCurrentBinary` returns downloads URL, `canAutoInstall` blocks prompt — consistent, no dead branch.

## Minor issues (non-blocking)

1. **Child killed by signal → exit 255, not 128+sig.** `updateflow.go:100` — child killed by SIGINT gives `ExitCode() = -1`, parent does `os.Exit(-1)` → 255. Shell loop won't break on Ctrl-C (main.go's `dieFromSignal` exists precisely for this). Also parent ctx cancel SIGKILLs child mid-cleanup (default `exec.CommandContext` Cancel). Edge case, low frequency — but a `WaitDelay`/`Cancel` override or signal-aware exit mapping would round it out.
2. **Substring match `IsCLIUpgradeRequired`.** Any error whose text contains `cli_upgrade_required` triggers takeover — e.g. server 500 body echoing the string. Comment explains why (auth-go has no sentinel); acceptable, but consider matching more anchored pattern (`oauth error: cli_upgrade_required`) if auth-go message shape is stable.
3. **`RerunCommandLine` quoting is Go-style, not shell.** Args with `$`, `*`, backticks pass unquoted — pasting back may re-expand. Display-only, tiny edge; fine to leave.
4. **`os.Exit` buried inside `RunUpdate`/`realReexecCommand`.** Skips `main.go`'s `cancel()`. Documented in doc comments ("does not return"), no deferred cleanup depends on it today — fine, just fragile if main ever grows deferred flush logic.

## Conventions & tests — good

- Accessibility: `NewAccessibleForm` used per CLAUDE.md convention. Non-interactive path prints complete copyable commands — agent-safe fallback rule satisfied.
- Seam-injection test pattern matches existing `autoupdate_test.go` style; `t.Parallel()` correctly omitted where package globals/env mutated, present elsewhere.
- Coverage thorough: detection, passthrough, non-interactive block, yes/no/decline, installer failure, re-exec failure, loop guard, argv reconstruction. Missing only trivial cases: stale-binary with empty argv (`"this binary"` fallback), and thin `OfferCLIUpgradeIfRequired` wiring — both fine to skip.
- No duplication: single `RunUpdate` implementation confirmed; refactor genuinely unifies the two triggers.

## Security

- Re-exec re-resolves `argv[0]` via `LookPath` — runs whatever PATH now points at, same trust model as installer itself. Env marker only additive. `sh -c` installer execution pre-existing. No new concerns.

## Verdict

Ship it. Design careful, loop guard well thought out, tests match implementation. Minor items above optional follow-ups — signal exit-code mapping (#1) most worth doing eventually.

Fix 1 (signal exit-code mapping + graceful cancel) and fix 4 (no `os.Exit` inside library — propagate exit code to main.go). Plan: `reexec` seam returns `(int, error)`, `RunUpdate` returns `(exitCode, exit bool)`, `OfferCLIUpgradeIfRequired` returns `(handled, exitCode)`, main.go owns the single `os.Exit`.

Both fixed. All tests green, lint clean (golangci-lint 2.11.3, 0 issues). Not committed — say when.

## Fix 1 — signal-aware exit codes + graceful cancel (`updateflow.go`)

- Signal-killed rerun child now maps to shell convention `128+signum` (SIGINT → 130) via `WaitStatus.Signaled()`, instead of `os.Exit(-1)` → 255. Weird `-1`-but-not-signaled falls back to 1.
- Ctrl-C no longer SIGKILLs child mid-cleanup: `cmd.Cancel` forwards `os.Interrupt`, `WaitDelay = 5s` hard-kills a child that ignores it. On Windows the Signal call fails and WaitDelay kill applies — same one code path.

## Fix 4 — no `os.Exit` buried in library

Exit moved to main.go's single exit point; deferred/cleanup in callers now always runs:

- `realReexecCommand` returns `(int, error)` — child exit code, or error when spawn failed.
- `RunUpdate` returns `(exitCode int, rerun bool)` — `rerun=true` means original command was re-executed and caller should exit with `exitCode`; `false` (nil argv, installer failure, spawn failure) means caller keeps its own path. Version-check caller (`MaybeAutoUpdate`) ignores returns — nil argv never reruns.
- `OfferCLIUpgradeIfRequired` returns `(handled bool, exitCode int)` — rerun child's code when update+retry ran, 1 on every other leaf.
- main.go: `exitCode := 1` before the switch, default arm overwrites when handled, single `cancel(); os.Exit(exitCode)`. Behavior unchanged on all failure leaves; successful update+retry still propagates child's code (including 0), now through main instead of deep inside `RunUpdate`.

## Tests

- Fixture `reexec` seam updated to `(int, error)`; added `reexecCode` field.
- New assertions: exit-code propagation through `RunUpdate` (child code 3) and through `offerCLIUpgrade` (exitCode 3 on accepted update, 1 on guidance leaves).
- New `TestRealReexecCommand_ExitCodes` (skipped on Windows): success → 0, `exit 3` → 3, SIGINT-killed → 130, unresolvable binary → error, nil argv → error. Exercises real spawn path including the new signal mapping.

Note: earlier IDE diagnostics referenced stale symbols (`errors.go` dup const, old test fields) — compiler and full test runs confirm tree is clean; those were LSP ghosts.

Manual test easy: fake auth server on loopback returning `cli_upgrade_required`, plus stub `curl` so no real install. Loopback `http://` is always allowed for `--server`, no insecure flag needed. Since fragment order matters here, full steps:

**1. Build test binary**

```fish
go build -o /tmp/entire-test ./cmd/entire
```

**2. Start fake auth server** (rejects device auth with the code; endpoint is `POST /device_authorization`)

```fish
python3 -c "
from http.server import HTTPServer, BaseHTTPRequestHandler
import json
class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        self.send_response(400)
        self.send_header('Content-Type','application/json')
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(json.dumps({'error':'cli_upgrade_required'}).encode())
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
HTTPServer(('127.0.0.1',8188),H).serve_forever()
" &
```

**3. Leaf: non-interactive guidance block** (kill switch forces it, works in any terminal)

```fish
env ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 /tmp/entire-test login --server http://127.0.0.1:8188 --device; echo $status
```

Expect: "This Entire CLI version is no longer supported. Update it:" + curl command + "Then rerun the command: entire-test login …", exit 1. Piping through `| cat` instead of the env var exercises the no-TTY gate.

**4. Leaf: stale-binary loop guard**

```fish
env ENTIRE_UPGRADE_RERUN=1 /tmp/entire-test login --server http://127.0.0.1:8188 --device; echo $status
```

Expect: "The update installed, but this command still ran an unsupported binary (/tmp/entire-test)…", no update offer, exit 1.

**5. Full interactive flow: prompt → fake install → auto-rerun → loop guard** (this exercises both fixes end-to-end). Stub `curl` so the dev build's `curl … | bash` installer runs harmlessly:

```fish
mkdir -p /tmp/fakebin
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "echo fake-install-ran"\n' > /tmp/fakebin/curl
chmod +x /tmp/fakebin/curl
env PATH="/tmp/fakebin:$PATH" /tmp/entire-test login --server http://127.0.0.1:8188 --device; echo $status
```

Answer **Yes** at the prompt. Expect sequence:

1. "Updating Entire CLI: curl -fsSL …" then `fake-install-ran` (stub output through bash),
2. "Update complete. Rerunning the command:",
3. child reruns, server rejects again, `ENTIRE_UPGRADE_RERUN=1` kicks in → stale-binary message,
4. `$status` = 1 — that's fix 4 working: child's exit code propagated through `RunUpdate` → `OfferCLIUpgradeIfRequired` → main.go's single `os.Exit`, no buried exit.

Answer **No** instead → printed commands leaf. Ctrl-C at prompt → same leaf.

**6. Fix-1 signal mapping** — awkward to trigger manually (rerun child fails instantly, no window to signal). Covered by `TestRealReexecCommand_ExitCodes`, which spawns real children: `sh -c "kill -INT $$"` → asserts 130. If want to see it live, one-liner against the real function:

```fish
go test ./cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/ -run TestRealReexecCommand_ExitCodes -v -count=1
```

Cleanup after: `kill %1` (fake server), `rm -rf /tmp/fakebin /tmp/entire-test`.

One note: step 5's prompt needs a real TTY — run it in your terminal directly, not through a pipe or agent subprocess.
